Why is the usage of the term "spyware" reduced in recent years?

Because it was a conscious decision by multiple groups to instead use the term "Malware" which more accurately describes Spyware, Viruses, and generally bad software, as "Malicious Software" or Malware for short. Basically, it confused the hell out of non-geeks when people had 10 different names for the same set of junk.

Because Malicious Software is a continuously changing market, and what we call "Viruses" now in 2016 have virtually nothing in common with the viruses we saw in say, 1989.

Spyware tended to be gray area applications that bundled themselves in with something else and monitored you for advertising purposes, or crammed ads into your browsing experience. It's still out there, it's just that in say... 2006, I'd be removing it every day of the week, but now in 2016, it's been more than a month since I've seen any on a client's machine.

Traditional Viruses and Spyware really kinda gave way to Scareware and Rootkits, and scareware (where they pretend to be a utility program/antivirus/the fbi/tech support) is mostly giving way to outright ransomware.
